subject: Intrinsic functions
notes: cite.py --check 15.3 'Locale-name. A locale-name defined in the SPECIAL-NAMES paragraph shall be specified' => OK §15.3 8). READ IntrinsicBinder.cs#BindLocaleFunction (dispatched at line 524 on `sig.ArgKinds.EndsWith('l')`, before the generic operand path): the leading positions bind as operands and the OPTIONAL LAST position is consumed as a NAME, resolved through DataBinder.ResolveLocaleName into the one LocaleRef; an undeclared name and a non-word in that position both draw COBOL1664, each message carrying the function's OWN rule (§15.51.3 r4 / §15.52.3 r3 / §15.53.3 r4 / §15.54.3 r2). The same resolver serves the other two locale-name sites — BindCaseFunctionWithLocale (the UPPER-CASE/LOWER-CASE LOCALE phrase) and BindNumvalCFamily (NUMVAL-C / TEST-NUMVAL-C LOCALE) — so there is ONE undeclared-locale-name diagnostic, not three. Absent, LocaleRef.Current applies (§14.6.6 r7/r8). The 'l' code carries its disposition in IntrinsicArgumentRules.NonOperandArgumentKinds, and IntrinsicArgumentClassDriftTests requires every catalog code to have either an Admissible arm or an entry there — so the name can never become the dead column §15.3 type 8 previously was (the catalog comment records that the column was unread while the rows bound as documented non-support). TESTS: 2014/pb64t4_locale_functions is the positive golden; pb64t4-locale-function-name-undeclared and pb64t5-case-phrase-name-undeclared pin the refusals.
